1. (Currently amended) An ultrasonic surgical instrument assembly comprising: a handpiece; a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece; a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; and a light source attached to said handpiece so as to direct at least visible electromagnetic radiation along the probe towards a surgical site distal of the probe, wherein said light source is positioned at a location other than that disclosed in Wuchinich US 5,176,677.

2. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1, further comprising a power supply mounted at least indirectly to said handpiece and operatively connected to said light source, wherein said power supply is configured to supply power independently to said light source separate from power supplied to said transducer or generator.

3. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2 wherein said power supply includes a coil disposed about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, and wherein said power supply is removably mounted to said handpiece via said coil.

4. (Original) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 3 wherein said power supply further includes a slow-drain capacitor for providing energy or power to said light source for a predetermined period of time after termination of power conduction through said cable.

5. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2, further comprising a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said handpiece, wherein said fastener comprises a clip, clamp, or band configured to secure said light source in a fixed position relative to said handpiece.

6. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 5, further comprising at least one additional fastener for removably attaching said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece, wherein said additional fastener is distinct from said fastener for said light source.

7. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2 wherein said power supply is a battery, and wherein said battery is removably mounted to said handpiece via a fastening mechanism.

8. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source includes a light-emitting diode, and wherein said light-emitting diode is operatively connected to a power source mounted on said handpiece.

9. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source is attached to a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising an optical fiber extending from said light source to a distal end portion of said handpiece, wherein said optical fiber is secured to said handpiece via at least one fastening element.

10. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source is attached to a distal end of said handpiece and is oriented to provide illumination along said probe to the surgical site, wherein said light source is positioned such that illumination is directed at an angle relative to the longitudinal axis of said probe.

11. (Currently amended) An accessory for a surgical instrument comprising a handpiece, a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece, and a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator, said accessory comprising: a light source; a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said handpiece, wherein said fastener comprises a clip, clamp, or band; and at least one power supply component operatively connectable to said light source, wherein said power supply component is configured to supply power independently to said light source.

12. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said power supply component includes a coil disposable about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, and wherein said power supply component is removably attachable to said handpiece via said coil, further comprising an additional fastener for removably securing said coil about the power cable.

13. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 12 wherein said power supply component further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil and connectable to said light source for providing illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable, wherein said capacitor is electrically isolated from said transducer or generator.

14. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said power supply component includes a battery, and wherein said battery is removably attachable to said handpiece via a fastening mechanism.

15. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said light source includes a light-emitting diode, and wherein said light-emitting diode is operatively connected to said power supply component.

16. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is configured for attaching said light source to a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising an optical fiber and at least one additional fastener for removably attaching said optical fiber to said handpiece so that said optical fiber extends from said light source to a distal end portion of said handpiece, wherein said optical fiber is secured along the length of said handpiece.

17. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is configured for attaching said light source to a distal end of said handpiece and for orienting said light source to provide illumination along said probe to a surgical site, wherein said light source is positioned to direct light at an angle relative to the longitudinal axis of said probe.

18. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is taken from the group consisting of a clip, a clamp, and a band, and wherein said fastener is configured to removably secure said light source without requiring tools for attachment or removal.

19. (Currently amended) A surgical method comprising: providing a surgical instrument having a handpiece, a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece and a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; providing a light source; applying a fastener to said handpiece to attach said light source thereto so that light from said light source is directed along said probe; operating said surgical instrument to apply ultrasonic vibratory energy to a surgical site; during the operating of said surgical instrument, conducting electrical energy from a power supply to said light source; and during the operating of said surgical instrument and the conducting of said electrical energy, illuminating said surgical site with light from said source.

20. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19 further comprising removably mounting said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece, wherein said power supply is mounted independently of said transducer or generator.

21. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 20 wherein said power supply includes a coil, the removable mounting of said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece including disposing said coil about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator and securing said coil via an additional fastener.

22. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 21 wherein said power supply further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil, further comprising operating said capacitor to provide illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable, wherein said capacitor supplies power independently to said light source.

23. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19, further comprising removing said fastener and said light source from said handpiece after completion of an operation on said surgical site, wherein said removal does not require disassembly of said handpiece.

24. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19 wherein the applying of said fastener includes positioning said light source at a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising attaching an optical fiber to said handpiece so that said fiber extends from said light source at said proximal end of said handpiece to a distal end of said handpiece, wherein said optical fiber is secured along the length of said handpiece via fastening elements.

25. (Currently amended) An accessory for a medical instrument comprising a handpiece and a probe or tool extension on a distal end of said handpiece, said accessory comprising: a light source; a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said instrument, wherein said fastener comprises a clip, clamp, or band; and at least one power supply component operatively connectable to said light source, said power supply component including a coil disposable about a power cable extending to said handpiece, wherein said power supply component is removably attachable to said handpiece via said coil, further comprising an additional fastener for removably securing said coil about the power cable.

26. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 25 wherein said power supply component further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil and connectable to said light source for providing illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable, wherein said capacitor supplies power independently to said light source.
